notes.md: - **Surajmal (Bharatpur):** Jat ruler of Bharatpur (ruled 1755-1763). A contemporary historian called him "the Plato of the Jat tribe" for his political wisdom.

new.s: Which regnal title did Aurangzeb assume?
new.x: Aurangzeb took the regnal title Alamgir, meaning 'World Conqueror'.
new.angle: U0133 notes gap: Aurangzeb regnal title Alamgir

new.s: Which musical instrument did Aurangzeb play, though he banned music at his court?
new.x: Aurangzeb banned court music, yet he played the veena himself.
new.angle: U0133 notes gap: Aurangzeb played the veena

new.s: In which year did the Satnami revolt break out at Narnaul?
new.x: The Satnamis of Narnaul (Haryana) rose in 1672 and were crushed.
new.angle: U0133 notes gap: Satnami revolt year 1672

new.s: Where did the Maratha Chhatrapati Rajaram die in 1700?
new.x: Rajaram, who resisted from Jinji, died at Sinhagad in 1700.
new.angle: U0133 notes gap: Rajaram died at Sinhagad

new.s: Maharaja Surajmal, described as 'the Plato of the Jat tribe', ruled which state?
new.x: Surajmal (ruled 1755-1763) was the Jat ruler of Bharatpur; a contemporary historian called him the Plato of the Jat tribe.
new.angle: U0133 web fact: Surajmal of Bharatpur - Plato of the Jat tribe (PYQ y44615cc88a3 angle)

new.s: Who was the executive and police officer at the pargana level in Mughal administration?
new.x: The Shiqdar headed the executive and police work of a pargana; the Faujdar worked at the sarkar level.
new.angle: U0134 notes gap: Shiqdar - pargana executive and police

new.s: Who was the village accountant in Mughal administration?
new.x: The Patwari was the village accountant; the Qanungo was head of the patwaris at pargana level.
new.angle: U0134 notes gap: Patwari - village accountant

new.s: Which Mughal revenue system was based on an estimate of the crop?
new.x: Kankut fixed revenue by estimating the standing crop; batai was crop-sharing.
new.angle: U0135 notes gap: Kankut - crop estimate

new.s: By which other name was the Subedar, the governor of a Mughal suba, known?
new.x: The Subedar, governor of a suba, was also called Nazim or Sipahsalar.
new.angle: U0135 notes gap: Subedar = Nazim

new.s: What were the provincial units of Qutb Shahi Golconda called?
new.x: Qutb Shahi Golconda was divided into tarafs and simalu.
new.angle: U0135 notes gap: Golconda units - tarafs

new.s: The zamindaris of which Andhra region date from the Qutb Shahi era?
new.x: The zamindars of the Northern Circars date from the Qutb Shahi period.
new.angle: U0135 notes gap: Northern Circars zamindars - Qutb Shahi era

new.s: Which centre in the Andhra-Telangana region was famous for Damascus swords?
new.x: Nirmal was known for Damascus swords.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Nirmal - Damascus swords

new.s: Which centre was famous for carpets and durries in the Qutb Shahi period?
new.x: Warangal was noted for carpets and durries.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Warangal - carpets and durries

new.s: Where is the Tobacco Board of India located?
new.x: The Tobacco Board is at Guntur; Andhra Pradesh is a top tobacco producer.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Tobacco Board at Guntur

new.s: In which year did Sir Thomas Roe come to the Mughal court?
new.x: Roe came in 1615; English ships reached Surat in 1608 and Hawkins got a firman in 1609.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Roe 1615

new.s: Who is the author of 'Storia do Mogor'?
new.x: Storia do Mogor was written by the Venetian Niccolao Manucci.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Storia do Mogor - Manucci

new.s: Which traveller wrote the 'Remonstrantie' on the reign of Jahangir?
new.x: The Dutch factor Francisco Pelsaert, who came in 1620, wrote the Remonstrantie.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Remonstrantie - Pelsaert

new.s: Which traveller wrote 'Six Voyages'?
new.x: The French diamond merchant Tavernier, who made six visits to India, wrote Six Voyages.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Six Voyages - Tavernier

new.s: Who is the author of 'Fall of the Mughal Empire'?
new.x: Fall of the Mughal Empire was written by Jadunath Sarkar.
new.angle: U0136 notes gap: Fall of the Mughal Empire - Jadunath Sarkar

new.s: Who was the only Mughal empress whose name appeared on coins?
new.x: Nur Jahan's name appeared on coins and farmans; she was the only empress so named on coins.
new.angle: U0137 notes gap: Nur Jahan - name on coins

new.s: In which year did Akbar abolish the jizya?
new.x: Akbar abolished the jizya in 1564, after abolishing the pilgrimage tax in 1563.
new.angle: U0137 notes gap: jizya abolished 1564

new.s: Which social practice did Akbar try to stop?
new.x: Akbar tried to stop forced sati; Bernier and Tavernier reported sati in Mughal India.
new.angle: U0137 notes gap: Akbar against forced sati

new.s: What was the original name of Mumtaz Mahal, for whom the Taj Mahal was built?
new.x: Mumtaz Mahal was Arjumand Banu Begum; Dilras Banu was Aurangzeb's wife and Mehr-un-Nissa was Nur Jahan.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Mumtaz Mahal = Arjumand Banu Begum

new.s: In which year was the Taj Mahal inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
new.x: The Taj Mahal and Agra Fort became UNESCO sites in 1983.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Taj Mahal UNESCO 1983

new.s: Which pair of Mughal monuments was inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1983?
o: Humayun's Tomb and Red Fort Complex
new.x: Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal were inscribed in 1983; Fatehpur Sikri in 1986, Humayun's Tomb in 1993, Red Fort in 2007.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: UNESCO 1983 - Agra Fort and Taj

new.s: In which year was the Taj Mahal declared one of the New Seven Wonders of the World?
new.x: The Taj Mahal was chosen among the New Seven Wonders in 2007.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Taj New Seven Wonders 2007

new.s: Which Mughal monument is known as the 'Baby Taj'?
new.x: Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb at Agra is called the Baby Taj; Bibi ka Maqbara is the Taj of the Deccan.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Baby Taj = Itimad-ud-Daula

new.s: For whom was the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula at Agra built?
new.x: It was built by Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg (Itimad-ud-Daula).
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Itimad-ud-Daula = Mirza Ghiyas Beg

new.s: Which monument has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture?
new.x: Humayun's tomb has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture; Sikandar Lodi's tomb had an earlier double dome.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: first Mughal double dome - Humayun's tomb

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Humayun's tomb has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture.
2. Sikandar Lodi's tomb had a double dome earlier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are true: Sikandar Lodi's tomb had an earlier double dome, and Humayun's tomb has the first full Persian double dome of the Mughals.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: double dome - Lodi and Humayun

new.s: How many storeys does the Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri have?
new.x: The Panch Mahal is a five-storeyed pillared building; its ground floor has 84 pillars.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Panch Mahal five storeys

new.s: What was the name of the new capital city founded by Shah Jahan at Delhi?
new.x: Shah Jahan built Shahjahanabad, with the Red Fort and Jama Masjid.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Shahjahanabad - Shah Jahan

new.s: Which city was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, on the Tungabhadra?
new.x: Hampi on the Tungabhadra was the Vijayanagara capital; Gulbarga was a Bahmani capital.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Vijayanagara capital Hampi

new.s: Where are the Qutb Shahi tombs, with onion domes on square bases, located?
new.x: The Qutb Shahi tombs stand at Ibrahim Bagh, Hyderabad.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh

new.s: Which is regarded as the first Mughal garden in India?
new.x: Babur's Ram Bagh at Agra is the first Mughal garden.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Ram Bagh first Mughal garden

new.s: Which Baluchi chief handed over Dara Shikoh to Aurangzeb?
new.x: Malik Jeevan handed Dara Shikoh over; he was killed in 1659.
new.angle: U0138 notes gap: Malik Jeevan handed over Dara
